subject: U.S. Route 101
hook: U.S. ROUTE 101 IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Despite its three-digit number, which usually denotes a spur route, U.S. Route 101 is actually a primary, major north-south highway that uses '10' as its first digit.
angle_support: Despite its three-digit number, normally used for spur routes, US 101 is classified as a primary route with 10 as its "first digit".
title: Why U.S. Route 101 isn't a spur route
description: Although its number suggests a secondary road, U.S. Route 101 is actually a major primary highway. It uses the first two digits to function as a main north-south route along the West Coast.
narration: U.S. ROUTE 101 IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture a minor spur route because of the three-digit name. It was never a side road. You see a primary highway that uses ten as its prefix. Under the federal numbering system, two-digit routes are primary. By treating the one-zero as the leading number, this road functions as a major north-south artery. It runs fifteen hundred miles along the Pacific, serving as a core corridor. The three-digit label is just a trick of the map.
